provenance.citation: Sussman, Gerald Jay. 'A Computational Model of Skill Acquisition.' MIT AI TR-297, 1973. The HACKER planner represents curriculum acquisition as a goal-atom state: each section is a goal atom; an already-mastered section appears as a matching initial-state fact (identity-matched by predicate=value, never by position).
provenance.locus: Chapter II, Sections 1-5: five Scenario curriculum sections as goals; two completed sections (CLEARTOP, bottom-up ordering) as identity-matched initial-state facts.
provenance.notes: Fixture encodes 5 curriculum goals as goal atoms (master=section-N) and 2 mastered sections as identity-matched facts (master=section-1, master=section-2). 3 goals remain unmastered; the HACKER curriculum step masters the lowest missing atom each step: 3 flips over 4 states. selected must equal '4 steps to goal'.

expected.rationale: 5 goal atoms, 2 identity-matched initial facts (master=section-1, master=section-2). 3 goals remain; each curriculum step masters the lowest missing goal atom: initial + 3 flips = 4 states. output.selected must equal '4 steps to goal'.
